title: StudyProtocol
description: An executable study protocol: what a study declares before it runs. The contract is closed (additionalProperties: false everywhere), mirroring #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on the Rust types in the sharpebench-study crate, and a bidirectional drift guard fails the build if the two disagree. No object in this schema can carry a result: there is no property for an achieved interval, an observed rate or a half width that was reached. A precision statement is derived from the runs actually executed, by the reporting path, and refused when those runs do not reach the required half width.

contract_version.description: The contract this document is written against. A field addition, removal or meaning change mints a new value rather than editing this one.

protocol_id.description: Stable identifier for this protocol across its versions. A changed value is a different protocol, not an amendment.

frozen.description: True once the document is sealed. Required on the frozen_validation tier and refused on the other two. An edit to a frozen protocol must raise its version.

claims.description: The claims the study is run to test. Empty only on the ci_regression tier, which tests pinned outputs rather than a claim.

estimands.description: The named quantities the study estimates. Outside the ci_regression tier at least one must be a per-entry or whole-field false-positive quantity; the two are separate estimands and are never conflated.

notes.description: Free text for the reader: provenance, caveats, and the decisions a placeholder document is still waiting on. Carries no meaning for the validator and no result.

ProtocolVersion.description: Ordered on (major, minor, patch). An amendment to a frozen protocol must raise it.

RunTier.description: ci_regression: pinned-output behaviour check; it cannot establish a rare false-positive rate or population power and may not carry a claim. development_calibration: exploratory, tuning permitted and recorded. frozen_validation: fixed method on reserved seeds, tuning refused, amendments must raise the version.

MethodIdentity.description: Which method, at which version, under which configuration. A study that cannot name the version it evaluated has no identity.

configuration_digest.description: Digest over the effective configuration document, lowercase hex.

scoring_spec_hash.description: Digest of the scoring specification the configuration resolves against.

EffectUnits.description: raw: arithmetic returns. active: returns net of the benchmark. The two are different quantities and one document reports one of them.

EstimandKind.description: Per-entry and whole-field false positives are separate variants because they are separate quantities.

EstimandTarget.description: An error-rate estimand takes an upper limit; a power estimand takes a lower bound. The crossed pairings are refused.

name.description: Unique within the protocol. Claims reference an estimand by this name.

DecisionRule.description: What would count as support for a claim, fixed before the data exists. A criterion for supporting a claim, not a requirement that the experiment produce a favourable result. unspecified is present so that omitting a rule is a refusable condition rather than a missing key.

statement.description: What is being asserted, bounded to the method version and configuration named in identity.

estimand.description: The name of the estimand this claim is decided on.

FieldComposition.description: Control entrants test refusal behaviour; they are not a substitute for a valid zero-skill null.

shared_market_history.description: True when entrants, windows or seeds are drawn from one market history. Those units are then repeated observations, not independent market replications.

SearchAssumptions.description: What the study assumes about the search that produced the entries it scores. An understated trial count understates the deflation.

DispersionPolicy.description: Whether the dispersion the deflation uses is a configured constant or measured from the field. The two give different answers and different failure modes.

null_family.description: The zero-skill generating process the error rates are measured against.

alternative_family.description: The generating process the power targets are measured against, including alternatives below and above the deflation benchmark.

tuning_allowed.description: Whether thresholds may be tuned against this tier's outputs. The frozen_validation tier refuses it.

ReplicationUnit.description: simulated_field is the only unit that stays independent when a market history is shared.

nested_observations.description: Units nested inside the independent one. Repeated or dependent observations, not counted in the denominator of an independent-replication rate.

ConfidenceLevel.description: Levels are enumerated rather than free-form so that every interval uses the same pinned normal quantile, checked against published values.

IntervalMethod.description: wilson_score: Wilson score interval for a binomial proportion. Named in the document so that a protocol assuming another construction is refused rather than silently reported under this one.

MultiplicityMethod.description: none is refused when more than one reported condition is predeclared.

Multiplicity.description: Predeclared across the conditions the study will report, so that a condition added afterwards is visibly an addition.

required_half_width.description: The half width the study requires of its reported interval. A requirement on the design, never a record of what was achieved.

Denominator.description: Which denominator a reason-coded outcome is counted against. Reporting conditional-on-availability results against the attempted denominator, or the reverse, is the silent denominator change this accounting prevents.

FailurePolicy.description: What the study does with a run that refuses, is unavailable, or fails on infrastructure. There is deliberately no variant that substitutes a zero return, a zero cost or a passing statistic for a missing result: an unavailable result is not a measurement. unspecified exists so that omission is refusable rather than absent.

Accounting.description: Expected counts and the handling of each way a run can fail to produce a result. Completed cannot exceed attempted, and available cannot exceed completed.

SimulationPlan.description: The simulation count and what it was sized for. The count is checked against the precision requirement by the validator; it is not taken on trust.

anticipated_rate.description: The rate the count is sized for. For a rare-event bound this is the target rate itself.

Budget.description: The resource and spend ceiling, and who approved it. A protocol whose estimates exceed its ceiling, or whose ceiling nobody approved, is refused before it can spend.

StoppingRule.description: Fixed by default. An adaptive rule is refused unless it states the error-control analysis that justifies it.

runs.description: Must equal the planned simulation count.
